Likelihood-Ratio Tests for Nested nbreg or zinbreg Fits

Source: R/inference.R
anova-nbzinbreg.Rd

Compares nested fits of the same class with likelihood-ratio tests: twice the difference in log-likelihoods, referred to a chi-squared distribution with degrees of freedom equal to the difference in the number of parameters. The fits are sorted by their number of parameters, and each is tested against the next smaller one.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
anova(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
anova(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbzinbreg_anova'
print(x, digits = max(getOption("digits") - 2L, 3L), ...)

Arguments

object

An nbreg or zinbreg fit.

...

Further fits of the same class, nested with object.

x

An nbzinbreg_anova table, for print().

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

Value

A data frame of class "anova" with one row per fit (sorted by the number of parameters): Model (the right-hand side of its formula), theta, Resid. df, 2 x log-lik., Test, df, LR stat., Pr(Chi) and Note, laid out like anova() of MASS::glm.nb fits.

Details

Checks before testing (each an nbzinbreg_error_input):

  • at least two fits, all of the same class. An nbreg fit and a zinbreg fit cannot be compared this way: the NB model is the boundary pi = 0 of the ZINB model, which the chi-squared reference does not cover. Use vuong_test() for that.

  • the same data: the same rows, response, weights and offsets;

  • strictly nested models: every column of each smaller model matrix (count and zero parts separately for zinbreg) lies in the column space of the next larger one, and no two fits have the same number of parameters.

Verification of the larger fit. The smaller fit is embedded exactly in the larger model, and the larger model is refitted from there. The algorithms never lower the log-likelihood, so this refit reaches at least the smaller fit's log-likelihood. If it beats the stored larger fit by more than 1e-6 * (|loglik| + 1), the stored fit is not at its maximum, and an nbzinbreg_error_fit is raised instead of a misleading test.

When no p-value is given. The chi-squared reference needs regular fits. If any fit in a comparison did not converge, has coefficients without a finite estimate, has theta on a bound, or (for zinbreg) has a collapsed zero part, the statistic is still shown but the p-value is NA, the Note column says why, and a warning is given (nbzinbreg_warning_convergence, _divergence or _theta).

Dropping zero-part covariates of a zinbreg model is an ordinary nested test. Removing the zero part entirely is not, because that is the boundary pi = 0; see vuong_test().

Errors and warnings

  • nbzinbreg_error_input: fewer than two fits, fits of different classes or not fits at all, fits to different data (rows, response, weights or offsets), models that are not nested, or two fits with the same number of parameters.

  • nbzinbreg_error_fit: a larger fit that is not at its maximum (its embedding refit is higher), or a negative statistic beyond rounding.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_convergence, nbzinbreg_warning_divergence, nbzinbreg_warning_theta: a fit in a comparison is not regular, so its p-value is NA (see the Note column).

See also

overdispersion_test(), vuong_test()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  m1 <- nbreg(art ~ fem + ment, data = bioChemists)
  m2 <- nbreg(art ~ fem + ment + kid5, data = bioChemists)
  anova(m1, m2)
}
#> Likelihood-ratio tests of negative binomial models
#> 
#> Response: art
#> 
#>               Model  theta Resid. df 2 x log-lik.   Test df LR stat.   Pr(Chi)
#> 1        fem + ment 2.1816       912      -3133.4                             
#> 2 fem + ment + kid5 2.2406       911      -3125.3 1 vs 2  1   8.1154 0.0043892
